rounds.text: EcoReco presents a compelling case of a high-growth business whose fundamental expansion has significantly outpaced its recent share price performance [E54]. While the market remains cautious, the company has demonstrated exceptional operational efficiency, with a 5-year compounded profit growth of 100% and a 3-year compounded sales growth of 40% [E15, E16, E19]. This performance is supported by superior capital allocation, evidenced by a ROCE of 30.8% and an ROE of 23.6%, both of which comfortably exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E10, E12, E13]. The company maintains a fortress balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.04x and a strong current ratio of 4.52x, ensuring it is effectively debt-free [E37, E38, E57]. Furthermore, the current market price sits below the intrinsic value calculated by a discounted cash flow model, which suggests a margin of safety of 21.9% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the stock is currently trading below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and debtor days have increased from 79.9 to 119 days [E50, E61]. Despite these short-term headwinds, the disconnect between the company's accelerating profit growth and its recent price decline suggests that sentiment has failed to keep pace with the underlying business reality [E55, E68].

Eco Recycling Ltd carries a demanding valuation across multiple metrics, trading at a P/E of 31.8x and a price-to-book ratio of 6.52x [E1, E2]. These multiples represent a steep premium compared to sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E sits at 16.65x and the sector P/B sits at 2.3x [E6, E7]. This premium extends to an EV/EBITDA of 20.4x against a sector benchmark of just 9.04x, while offering a negligible dividend yield of 0.23% [E4, E11]. Furthermore, longer-term fundamental progress shows a stark contrast, as compounded sales growth over a 10-year period languishes at a meager 3% [E14]. Operational warning signs are visible in the cash conversion ratio of 0.57x for March 2026, indicating that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation and pointing to potential issues with receivables or accruals [E34]. This is corroborated by debtor days expanding significantly from 79.9 to 119 days [E61]. Market sentiment and momentum are also weak, with the 1-year compounded share price growth sitting at -27% [E25], the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], and foreign institutional holdings declining from 0.90% in December 2023 to 0.25% in September 2026 [E42]. Conceded: [E19] and [E20], which show strong 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth of 100% and 79% respectively, alongside robust return metrics such as an ROCE of 26.52% versus a sector benchmark of 17.57% [E10].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E4], [E6], [E7], [E11], [E14], [E25], [E42], [E50], and [E61]. The premium valuation multiples and rising debtor days are heavily outweighed by exceptional fundamental acceleration, where 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth reached 100% and 79% respectively, massively outstripping the sector median profit growth of 23.4% [E19, E20, E70]. This earnings surge is supported by top-tier capital efficiency, with a 26.52% ROCE and 20.46% ROE that easily surpass sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. The business is generating tangible financial returns, producing Rs 13 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 12 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 while maintaining a virtually debt-free balance sheet with a 0.04x debt-to-equity ratio [E35, E36, E37, E57]. Furthermore, the market price of Rs 429 sits below a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 549, providing a 21.9% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Fundamentals are clearly outpacing the stock price, creating a disconnect where results are scoring 92/100 with accelerating 34% YoY net profit growth while sentiment remains overly cautious [E54, E64, E68].

Conceded: [E35], [E36], [E37], [E57]. The bull highlights stellar profit growth rates of 100% over 5 years and 79% over 3 years [E19, E20], but completely ignores the structural stagnation evidenced by a meager 3% compounded sales growth over 10 years [E14]. While ROCE and ROE beat benchmarks [E9, E10], the company's valuation metrics—such as a P/E of 29.59x to 31.8x, P/B of 6.11x to 6.52x, and EV/EBITDA of 20.4x—trade at massive premiums over sector benchmarks of 16.65x, 2.3x, and 9.04x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11]. Furthermore, the impressive reported earnings are heavily undermined by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.57x for March 2026, which clearly indicates that profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation [E34]. This liquidity disconnect is compounded by soaring debtor days, which have escalated sharply from 79.9 to 119 days [E61].
